payload.source_label: The acoustics matrix in (1.6) has eigenvalues -c and +c

contract.statement: For the constant real acoustics matrix A = [[0, K], [1/ρ, 0]], where K is the material's bulk modulus and ρ its density, define c = √(K/ρ) as the sound speed [printed p. 2, (1.6) and following discussion]. The selected source sentence states that A has eigenvalues −c and +c and that these are the acoustic propagation speeds in the one-dimensional medium [printed p. 3, opening paragraph]. The preceding characteristic equations identify +c with rightward travel and −c with leftward travel [printed p. 2, discussion of w¹ and w²]. The physical parameter domain is implicit; explicit positivity inequalities and degenerate cases are not supplied in this passage [printed p. 2, material-parameter paragraph and sound-speed discussion].
assumptions: A is specifically the constant-coefficient acoustics matrix of (1.6) for the one-dimensional material described by K and ρ [printed p. 2, (1.5)–(1.6); printed p. 3, selected sentence].

The source uses a real sound speed and the coefficient 1/ρ; ordinary real interpretation therefore requires a defined reciprocal and real square root. These domain requirements are inferred from the displayed expressions, not stated as explicit inequalities in the selected passage [printed p. 2, (1.6) and c = √(K/ρ)].
The enclosing framework is a homogeneous first-order system q_t + A q_x = 0 with constant real coefficients [printed p. 1, (1.1) and following paragraph].
The acoustic example models waves in both directions along a one-dimensional medium [printed p. 2, introduction to (1.5)].
The preceding discussion relates a complete family of real eigenvectors to decomposition into waves and identifies eigenvalues with propagation speeds [printed p. 3, opening paragraph].

Positive sound speed is part of the preceding physical discussion of a wave traveling to the right with c > 0; the selected matrix sentence does not independently state positivity assumptions on K or ρ [printed p. 2, introduction to (1.4), and paragraph after (1.5); printed p. 3, selected sentence].
quantifiers: K and ρ are the constant material parameters, respectively bulk modulus of compressibility and density; the passage introduces them descriptively rather than with an explicit universal quantifier [printed p. 2, paragraph after (1.5)].
A is the 2 × 2 real matrix [[0, K], [1/ρ, 0]] [printed p. 2, (1.6); printed p. 1, real-matrix convention after (1.1)].
c is defined by c = √(K/ρ) [printed p. 2, immediately after w¹ = p + ρcu].
